chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Harun ibn Hamzah from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "What has become of Umar ibn Muslim?" I said: "May I be your ransom, he has turned to worship and left trade."
He said: "Woe to him, does he not know that the one who abandons seeking (livelihood) will not have his prayers answered?"

Indeed, a group from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when this verse was revealed: 'And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect.'
"And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect."

They closed their doors and turned to worship, saying: 'We have been provided for.' This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), so he sent for them and said: "What compelled you to do what you did?"
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, You promised us our livelihood, so we turned to worship."
He said: "Indeed, whoever does that will not have his prayers answered; it is upon you to seek (livelihood)."
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet tell his companions to stop abandoning trade for worship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the example of Umar ibn Muslim to illustrate the error of passive reliance (tawakkul) without effort, noting that some Companions closed their shops to worship after hearing the verse about provision from unexpected sources. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) corrected this misconception, clarifying that 'being sufficient' requires active pursuit (al-talab), as those who abandon seeking sustenance will not have their prayers answered. This hadith establishes the Shia jurisprudential principle that spiritual devotion must be coupled with economic activity, rejecting the notion that worship exempts one from the duty of earning a livelihood.
